notes: The villager sheet is composed at runtime (sheetFor/partsFor in index.html) from the villager atlas (chars/atlas.png, built from chars/layers/ by tools/art/pack.py): 9 columns x 4 rows (rows = facing). Anchor = the feet. Frame indexes are columns within the facing's row. walk_<facing>: the LPC frames already dip the head 1 px on one frame per step (indexes 2 and 6 facing up/down, 0 and 4 facing left/right); those frames hold longer (the weight lands) and `lift` (sheet px, eased between frames in code) is 0 there and highest at the passing frames. `walk` is the old even cycle, kept for the before/after GIF. motion: rows above `split` are the upper body; `stop` squashes it (px down, eased through the keys) when a villager stops; `breath` lifts it 1 px now and then while standing; `hair` is a spring (stiffness, damping, sideways kick on a stop) the hair layer follows the head with; each villager walks at a speed in `speed` and is up to `phase_ms` out of step, both from its name.
